messages:
deploy-bot: kicking off staged rollout: service=redwood-infer-api version=2.3.1 -> initial 10% traffic across global clusters. change-window=2024-11-07T22:00Z. ping if any immediate issues. :rocket:
sara: watching metrics now. loading dashboards...
matt: saw small uptick in eu-west tail latency ~3m after cutover, grabbing raw logs.
ops-oncall: can you paste the metric snapshot? need baseline vs now.
sara: Canary metrics (last 5m): 5xx_rate global 0.8% -> 2.9%, eu-west 5xx 0.4% -> 5.6%. p50 latency unchanged, p99 up from 210ms -> 520ms.
kai: uh - looks like edge eu-west-2 pods returning tokenizer exceptions in short prompt path. sample log: `ERROR tokenization: unknown token id -1
  at model/encoder.py:142`
lucy: is this the v2.3.1 tokenizer change? release diff showed a serialized vocab bump.
matt: yep. the model variant we shipped included tokenizer update that wasn't backwards compatible with cached requests. some requests hitting KV cache cause decode exceptions.
ops-oncall: recommend PAUSE rollout and pin EU traffic to v2.3.0 while we confirm scope.
sara: agree. can we do a regional pin rather than full rollback? EU only.
deploy-bot: rollout status: 10% deployed (global). region breakdown: eu-west=3%, us-east=4%, ap-south=3%. To pause run: `/deploy pause --id=rollout-1765432100`
ops-oncall: running pause now.
ops-oncall: `/deploy pause --id=rollout-1765432100` -> accepted. Rolling back regional routing for eu-west to pinned version v2.3.0.
deploy-bot: action: route override applied. eu-west traffic now pinned to v2.3.0 (3% total). Verified: 200 OK from health-check endpoints.
release-eng: adding to release notes: "hotfix required: tokenizer compatibility issue detected in v2.3.1; EU traffic pinned to v2.3.0 while we investigate."
lucy: I'll open a hotfix branch, revert tokenizer serialization, add regression unit test for cached decode path.
kai: posting a repro: curl to internal test harness -> `curl -X POST https://int-test/eu/infer -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H 'X-Model-Version:2.3.1'` yields 500 with tokenizer error. cc @matt
matt: running canary-runner against 2.3.1 with short prompts reproduces locally. capturing stacktrace and will attach to GH issue.
sara: ops, confirm that there are no user-facing incidents. Any customer reports?
ops-oncall: no support tickets yet. error spike small but unsafe if grows. pinning prevents further exposure.
release-eng: schedule: hotfix branch today, run quick canary in staging, target redeploy v2.3.2 tomorrow morning US window. update channel when ready.
kai: for transparency adding telemetry quick fix: fallback to old tokenizer on cache decode failures and log once per minute. cheap mitigation.
lucy: good. will include test and revert once proper fix shipped.
sara: re-checking metrics after pin: eu-west 5xx dropping from 5.6% -> 0.6% within 60s. nice.
matt: thanks team. After hotfix lands, let's plan a controlled re-roll with 1% sample in EU first and extended monitoring for 30m.
release-eng: I'll update release notes and tag customers if needed. Also adding a brief postmortem template: cause, mitigation (pin), follow-up (fix and regression test), lessons learned.
ops-oncall: closing the immediate action. if we see re-escalation we revert global rollout. :white_check_mark:
sara: ack. good catch everyone.
deploy-bot: rollout paused by ops-oncall. current global deployed fraction: 7% (EU pinned to 2.3.0).
